summary: Redwood (AE+SE) reviewed SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture with Brookside Health security and compliance stakeholders. Discussed availability of reports via Trust Center, controls mapping for Brookside's audit scope, RBAC and SSO integration, audit log export/retention needs, KMS/encryption and key separation options, and data residency/VPC deployment constraints. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share Trust Center artifacts and controls mapping, schedule technical deep dive to validate audit log exports and KMS integration, Brookside to share in-scope systems and residency requirements.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sam Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Robinson (CISO, Brookside), Marta Diaz (Head of Compliance), Jamal Price (Cloud Ops)

[00:00] Sam Lee: Hi everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining. This is Sam from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:10] Alex Robinson: Good, thanks. Alex here. Appreciate you fitting us in. We wanted to run through SOC 2 and ISO posture and make sure the artifacts line up with our procurement needs.
[00:20] Sam Lee: Absolutely, that's the plan. Priya, want to kick us off with a quick overview of the artifacts we typically surface in the Trust Center?
[00:30] Priya Nair: Sure, yeah. So we have SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO 27001 certificate, and then a controls mapping doc that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks. We also provide a Trust Center link where authorized customers can download the artifacts and request NDA-protected access to sensitive evidence.
[00:46] Marta Diaz: When you say "controls mapping" is that the detailed mapping to our scope, or is it more of a high level? For an audit we need control IDs and evidence links ideally.
[00:55] Priya Nair: Great question. The controls mapping we share is fairly detailed — it maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 criteria and ISO annex A sections. For customers doing an in-depth review we can provide a redacted evidence index, and for full evidence we handle through a legal/secure process (NDA + Trust Center elevated access).
[01:12] Jamal Price: And the Trust Center link, is that self-serve or do we need to open a support ticket to get access?
[01:18] Sam Lee: It's self-serve to an extent — standard artifacts are available with an account, but access to sensitive evidence or baked artifacts requires an access request. We can create a request on your behalf.
[01:27] Alex Robinson: Cool. Timeline — we expect to have procurement review next week. We need SOC 2 Type II and ISO cert before legal signs off. Are those current?
[01:36] Priya Nair: Yes, SOC 2 Type II is current through 2024-12 and ISO 27001 certificate is active as of 2025-03. We'll share the exact dates in the artifact metadata.
[01:45] Marta Diaz: Any material exceptions in the SOC 2?
[01:48] Priya Nair: No material exceptions. There are minor findings in change management process notes from late 2023 but those were remediated; the auditor notes are included.
[01:58] Alex Robinson: Okay good. On the technical side, audit logs: we want to be able to export all admin activity and API request logs to our SIEM and retain for 1 year. What options do you support?
[02:09] Priya Nair: We support streaming audit logs to customer-owned S3 buckets or syslog endpoints; we also offer push integrations to common SIEMs. Retention is configurable on your side once you ingest logs. We retain operational logs for 90 days in Redwood, but for long-term retention you should export to your storage.
[02:28] Jamal Price: When you say "operational logs" what's included? Admin console activity, model invocation metadata, error logs?
[02:36] Priya Nair: Admin console events, user provisioning, role changes, API keys, and high-level invocation metadata (timestamps, model id, request id, token counts). For privacy we don't include full prompt contents in operational logs unless you enable request logging explicitly for a given project; payload logging is off by default.
[02:58] Alex Robinson: We need to ensure we can capture request metadata but not PII. Will your export allow column-level filtering?
[03:05] Priya Nair: Yes, exports are configurable — you can include or exclude specific fields. We also provide redaction tools in the pipeline if you want to scrub PII before it hits your bucket.
[03:17] Sam Lee: Quick note on encryption: Redwood encrypts data at rest and in transit. For enterprise customers we support customer-managed keys (KMS) so keys can be in your cloud provider or via HSM. Priya, do you want to add the key separation details?
[03:30] Priya Nair: Sure. With customer-managed keys, you control rotation and revocation. For our hosted customers we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault integrations. For dedicated/private we can do a bring-your-own-key model with HSM-backed key stores. There are operational caveats to revoking keys with in-flight cached KV data — we can document the process.
[03:52] Jamal Price: Important — if we rotate keys will it invalidate cached KV caches or cause downtime?
[03:58] Priya Nair: There is a short window for rekeying; our ops procedures handle rewrapping cache entries to avoid downtime, but that requires coordination and a maintenance window for Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted we have managed rotation with minimal impact but we'll provide the runbook.
[04:15] Alex Robinson: Great. On RBAC and SSO: we use SAML SSO with SCIM for provisioning. We need role-based separation for compliance reviewers vs. engineers. How granular are your roles?
[04:26] Sam Lee: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls with built-in roles plus custom role creation. You can scope roles to projects and models, and set permissions for viewing logs, downloading artifacts, and performing admin actions.
[04:39] Marta Diaz: Are audit events logged when roles change and SSO provisioning events occur?
[04:44] Priya Nair: Yes, those events are included in the admin audit stream and will be part of the export.
[04:49] Alex Robinson: Data residency — Brookside requires PHI data to remain in US regional boundaries. Can Redwood guarantee that?
[04:57] Priya Nair: We provide region pinning for models and data processing in specific cloud regions. For Hosted we have US regions; we can ensure data processing in a US region. For stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where network and storage are fully isolated.
[05:14] Jamal Price: For Dedicated, do we get full control of network egress and ability to put it inside our VPC?
[05:20] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated includes VPC peering or private link options and you can restrict egress. Private deployment gives you full on-prem or VPC-only control.
[05:27] Alex Robinson: Sounds good. For the controls mapping — can you show an example of the mapping artifact?
[05:33] Sam Lee: We'll share a sample. Priya do you have the mapping open?
[05:37] Priya Nair: I do, I'm pulling a redacted copy. For example control CC6 in SOC 2 maps to our change control policy, change tickets, and deployment audit logs. For ISO A.12.1 we map to operational procedures and monitoring. The mapping is a table with control ID, description, Redwood control references, and evidence links.
[05:57] Marta Diaz: When you say "evidence links" those are the auditor artifacts or internal logs? We need to see auditor evidence for a subset.
[06:06] Priya Nair: Auditor evidence is redacted typically; full evidence is available via the Trust Center under elevated access. The mapping will indicate where evidence is stored and how to request it.
[06:16] Alex Robinson: Any third-party pen tests or bug bounty results that are shared?
[06:21] Priya Nair: We publish summary results and remediation timelines; detailed reports are available under NDA. We also list our pentest vendors and frequency.
[06:30] Jamal Diaz: Encryption in transit — do you support TLS 1.3 and mutual TLS for some endpoints?
[06:36] Priya Nair: Yes TLS1.3 by default; mutual TLS is available for Private/Dedicated and for certain customer endpoints.
[06:43] Alex Robinson: What about logging of prompts — you said request payloads are off by default. Our legal team may want redacted transcripts for a subset. Is selective logging supported?
[06:55] Sam Lee: Yes selective logging is supported per project; you can enable payload logging and apply redaction rules. We recommend using a redaction pipeline to remove PII before storage.
[07:06] Jamal Price: Ok, on the technical follow-up, we want to test pushing audit logs to our S3 bucket, validate field-level filtering, and simulate KMS rotation. Can we get a test account?
[07:18] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll provision a sandbox org for that. Priya: action item to schedule and provide runbooks.
[07:25] Sam Lee: I'll own the Trust Center artifacts share and controls mapping.
[07:29] Alex Robinson: For procurement, pricing and SLAs matter — do you have SOC-related SLAs or data residency SLAs?
[07:37] Sam Lee: Our Dedicated agreements include uptime and latency SLAs; data residency is covered contractually for Dedicated/Private. Hosted API has standard TOS; we can escalate to legal for residency clauses.
[07:49] Marta Diaz: Any certifications for people handling data — background checks, least privilege policies?
[07:55] Priya Nair: Yes, our staff handling production systems are background checked as part of hiring, and we enforce least privilege and periodic access reviews. That is covered in the SOC 2 description.
[08:05] Alex Robinson: One more Q on retention: Redwood retains user data for 30 days by default, is that right?
[08:11] Priya Nair: For hosted we have default retention windows for prompt buckets; we can configure shorter or longer retention for enterprise customers, and Dedicated/Private behaves per customer policy. We'll confirm the exact defaults in the artifact.
[08:24] Sam Lee: Let's go through the agreed deliverables. Quick recap: Sam will share Trust Center link and controls mapping; Priya will schedule the technical deep dive sandbox and runbook; Brookside to send list of in-scope apps and residency constraints. Anything else?
[08:38] Alex Robinson: Can you also include a sample SLA and the encryption rekeying runbook?
[08:44] Sam Lee: Yes I'll include sample SLA and the rekeying runbook for Dedicated/Hosted differences.
[08:50] Marta Diaz: We'll want to review the controls mapping with our auditors; can you add a row-level description so auditors can map quickly?
[08:58] Priya Nair: We can add auditor-facing comments in the mapping.
[09:03] Jamal Price: For the sandbox, we will need credentials and a time window next week. We'll propose Wed or Thu.
[09:10] Sam Lee: Noted, we'll propose Wed morning.
[09:13] Alex Robinson: Any competing products we should be aware of? Our procurement asked about BigCloudAI and ModelServeCo; your differentiator on inference economics is interesting but we need the compliance posture to match those vendors.
[09:25] Sam Lee: Understood — on compliance we aim to be parity or better; we can provide a competitor controls comparison snapshot.
[09:33] Marta Diaz: One last operational question — how do you handle subpoena or legal requests for customer data?
[09:39] Priya Nair: Subpoena responses are handled by our legal team; we notify customers and follow contract terms and local law. For Private deployments where data is customer-managed we have no rights to customer content.
[09:54] Alex Robinson: Ok that covers it for now. Let's confirm the timeline: trust center artifacts by Tue EOD, sandbox schedule Wed, controls mapping in the ShareDoc by next Tue?
[10:07] Sam Lee: We'll target that; Sam: confirm timeline in follow-up email.
[10:12] Priya Nair: I'll set up the sandbox and calendar invite.
[10:16] Alex Robinson: Thanks everyone.
[10:18] Sam Lee: Thanks Alex, Marta, Jamal — we'll follow up with the items.

[30:00] -- mid-call chitchat and minor interruptions, background noise --

[40:00] -- end of meeting wrap and confirmation of next steps --

End transcript.
